title: Не будь тряпкой  (Don't Be a Pushover)

segments.t: In the kitchen, Senya and Fedya are staging a ridiculous mock execution for a fish instead of preparing orders. Katya snaps at them to get back to work, and when Denis fusses over her with sweet pet names, she loses her patience with him too. Let's listen to the confrontation in Russian.
Может, мы уже работать начнём?
Да, сейчас мы уже начнём.
Я сказала вам быстро работать!
Катюша, ну не нервничай так.
Денис, слушай, мы сейчас на работе.
Федя, ну не нервничай ты так.
Зачем ты сейчас это делаешь?
Катюша, прошу тебя, просто успокойся.
Не называй ты меня тут Катюшей!
Перестань вести себя как тряпка.
Мне такие мальчики совсем не нравятся.
Я же просто хотел тебе помочь.
Now let's examine why Katya loses her temper with Denis in the kitchen line by line.
Может, мы уже работать начнём?
'Maybe we will start working already?' Katya interrupts the pranksters with a modal word and a first-person plural future verb.
Да, сейчас мы уже начнём.
'Yes, we will start right now.' Senya promises immediate action by repeating the perfective future verb without the infinitive.
Я сказала вам быстро работать!
'I told you to work quickly!' A feminine past verb of speaking with an infinitive expresses a firm command.
Катюша, ну не нервничай так.
'Katyusha, come on, do not be so nervous.' Denis tries to soothe her in front of the cooks using an affectionate diminutive and negated imperative.
Денис, слушай, мы сейчас на работе.
'Denis, listen, we are at work right now.' She reminds him of their professional setting using the prepositional case for being at work.
Федя, ну не нервничай ты так.
'Fedya, come on, do not be so nervous.' Senya mocks Denis's gentle tone by repeating the exact same phrase to his partner Fedya.
Зачем ты сейчас это делаешь?
'Why are you doing this right now?' After Katya retaliates against Senya's prank, Denis asks a startled question in the present tense.
Катюша, прошу тебя, просто успокойся.
'Katyusha, I beg you, just calm down.' A reflexive perfective imperative urges Katya to regain her composure.
Не называй ты меня тут Катюшей!
'Do not call me Katyusha in here!' The negated verb of naming takes an accusative direct object and an instrumental predicate name.
Перестань вести себя как тряпка.
'Stop behaving like a pushover.' Literally meaning rag, the feminine noun is used idiomatically for a weak-willed person or doormat.
Мне такие мальчики совсем не нравятся.
'I do not like boys like that at all.' A negated plural reflexive verb of liking takes a dative experiencer and nominative plural subject.
Я же просто хотел тебе помочь.
'I just wanted to help you.' Denis defends his intentions with a masculine past verb and a perfective infinitive taking the dative. Let's hear the kitchen argument again from beginning to end.

Katya hates being coddled at work and warns Denis that she does not date spineless boys. Listen for the reflexive imperatives meaning don't be nervous and calm down. See you in the next scene.
Перестань вести себя как тряпка.
